title: Offensive Language Detection: A Comparative Analysis
answer_short: The RKS approach explicitly maps data vectors to a space where linear separation is possible, providing an approximate kernel function via explicit mapping, and was used to improve evaluation scores in offensive language detection by mapping embedding vectors to higher dimensions for linear separability.
answer_rationale: The Random Kitchen Sink (RKS) approach is described as a method that explicitly maps data vectors to a space where linear separation is possible, providing an approximate kernel function via explicit mapping. It was applied in this context to improve classification scores by mapping embedding vectors (from Google universal sentence encoder and Fasttext) to higher dimensions (up to 1000), achieving high accuracy (e.g., 99.53% for Fasttext). This method was used to enhance the discriminative capability of features, making them linearly separable in higher-dimensional space, which improved overall performance.
